title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-18
source: Audience Cassette->Nakamichi Dragon->Sony PCMR300 Dat (16/44.1)->Sound Forge eq and normalization

ai_review.summary: A stellar audience recording that captures an incendiary second set – Dark Star, Let It Grow and more – with astonishing clarity and instrument separation.
ai_review.review: Listeners rave about the crystal‑clear audience tape that rivals many soundboard releases, noting superb spatial imaging and a warm mix where Bob Weir often dominates in a glorious fashion. The show’s second set is repeatedly called “epic,” featuring Dark Star, Eyes of the World, China Rider, Wharf Rat/Row Jimmy and an unforgettable Let It Grow performance. Minor balance quirks (bass/piano low on some sections) do not detract from the overall brilliance.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both performance and recording across 8 of 9 reviews; minor balance issues are outweighed by the show’s legendary second‑set and exceptional audience sound.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Exceptionally clear, minimal crowd noise, superb instrument separation; occasional balance problems (bass/piano low early, drums a touch subdued) but overall spacious and clean.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The second set is highlighted as a seamless, high‑energy journey that many reviewers call one of the best ever; transitions flow naturally and the band stays on fire throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s playing is solid and audible; some listeners note he isn’t as forward as Weir but his tone remains strong.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass described as fat, swampy and powerful despite occasional low‑level presence in the mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir dominates the mix with hot, complex, and “unhinged” playing—especially on Let It Grow—earning high praise for his guitar work and vocals.
band_member_comments.Keys: Piano is sparse and often hard to hear; reviewers acknowledge its minimal presence but feel it doesn’t hurt the overall performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming praised as “drilling” and a highlight of the show; no second drummer (Mickey Hart) present, which some note positively.
